harmonization.label: Blues
harmonization.description: 7th chords and a shuffle groove, following the shape of the 12-bar blues.

changes: Ends by walking down the home chord to C4.
Built on the C blues scale, played in one hand position around frets 8–11.
Odd bars follow the shape of your tune; even bars answer it — the call-and-answer of a real solo.
Every technique is switched on, whatever your level.
Bends (b): push the string towards the ceiling until it sounds like the note shown — use two or three fingers together.
Slides (/): keep pressing and glide your finger up the string to the new fret.
Bend and release (b…r): bend up, then let the string come back down while it rings.
Vibrato (~): rock the bend a tiny bit up and down to make a held note sing.
This part sits higher up the neck than the easy solo, but your hand stays put around fret 8.

guide.title: 12-bar blues
guide.body: The blues follows a 12-bar map: four bars of I, two of IV, two of I, then V – IV – I – V to turn around and start again.

guide.title: Dominant 7th chords
guide.body: Blues plays I, IV and V all as 7th chords (C7, F7, G7). The extra ♭7 gives that unresolved, gritty sound.

guide.title: Shuffle feel
guide.body: In a shuffle, the second eighth note of each beat comes late — long-short, long-short — like a heartbeat: ta-da, ta-da.

guide.title: The blue note
guide.body: The blues scale adds the ♭5 to the minor pentatonic. Bending the ♭3 halfway towards the 3rd is the most famous blues sound.
